#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A stand-in for the claude, codex and gemini command-line tools (it answers by the name it is run as).

It reads the prompt on stdin and answers the way tests/sim.py would. FAKE_CLI_PROSE names seats whose
FIRST answer is prose instead of JSON, so tests can drive the reject -> retry -> accept path.
FAKE_CLI_DOWN names tools that fail the way a logged-out tool does.
It checks only that our adapters hold together; it says nothing about the real tools.
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import zlib
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, os.environ["FAKE_CLI_TESTS"])
import sim  # noqa: E402

name = Path(sys.argv[0]).stem
for _stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
    _stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
prompt = sys.stdin.buffer.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
if name in os.environ.get("FAKE_CLI_DOWN", "").split(","):           # a tool that is installed but logged out
    print(f"not logged in: run `{name} login` first", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(3)
if "Reply with exactly the two letters" in prompt:                 # doctor --probe
    reply = "OK"
else:
    seat = sim.seat_of(prompt)
    state = Path(os.environ["FAKE_CLI_STATE"]) / f"{seat}.{zlib.crc32(prompt.splitlines()[0].encode())}"
    first = not state.exists()
    state.write_text("seen", encoding="utf-8")
    if first and seat in os.environ.get("FAKE_CLI_PROSE", "").split(","):
        reply = "Sure! I had a careful look at the packet and here are my thoughts in plain prose."
    elif "· CODEBASE MAP ·" in prompt:                              # the mapper answers with a document
        reply = sim.codebase_map(prompt)
    else:
        reply = json.dumps(sim.answer(prompt))
if name == "codex":                                                  # codex exec ... -o <file> ... -
    Path(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("-o") + 1]).write_text(reply, encoding="utf-8")
    print("tokens used: 1234")
elif name == "gemini":                                               # gemini -o json -p <nudge>
    print(json.dumps({"response": reply, "stats": {}}))
else:                                                                # claude -p --output-format text
    print(reply)

"""Write tests/fixtures/yaml_dump.json: documents and how PyYAML's safe_dump spells them.

The Rust YAML writer is a port of PyYAML's emitter. Its unit test reads this file and must produce
the same text for every case, byte for byte. Re-run this script after adding cases:

    python3 tests/make_yaml_fixture.py
"""
import json
import random
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

WORDS = ("queue retries idempotent ledger shard cache index batch stream replay quorum backoff tenant schema rollout canary "
         "metric budget latency replica snapshot throttle circuit fallback audit").split()
TEXTS = [
    "", " ", "a", "plain text", " leading", "trailing ", "two  spaces", "x: y", "x:y", "a #b", "a#b", "#start", "- item", "-item", "-",
    "? q", "?q", ": c", ":c", "[x]", "{x}", "a, b", "a [b] {c}", "&anchor", "*alias", "!tag", "|", ">", "'quoted'", '"double"', "it's",
    "%percent", "@at", "`tick`", "---", "--- doc", "...", "... end", "null", "Null", "~", "true", "False", "yes", "No", "on", "OFF", "y", "n",
    "123", "0x1F", "010", "1_000", "+5", "-7", "1.5", ".5", "1e3", "1.0e+3", "1:30", ".inf", "-.INF", ".NaN", "<<", "=", "2026-11-13",
    "2026-11-13 10:00:00", "2026-11-13T10:00:00Z", "2026-1-3", "12:30", "v1.2.3", "fanout:claude", "Claude Fable 5.2 (max)",
    "current model @ high", "C:\\Users\\me\\My Vault", "/home/me/a b/c", "tab\there", "line\nbreak", "two\n\nbreaks", "ends with break\n",
    "\nstarts with break", "space \nbreak", "break\n space", "caf\u00e9", "\u2192 arrow", "emoji \U0001f600", "nbsp\u00a0here", "bell\x07",
    "back\\slash", 'quote " inside', "both ' and \"", "a: b: c", "key:", "url http://example.org/a?b=c#d", "100%", "a&b", "a*b", "a|b", "a>b",
    "x" * 130, " ".join(WORDS), " ".join(WORDS * 6), "note: " + " ".join(WORDS * 6), "it's " + " ".join(WORDS * 6),
    "caf\u00e9 " + " ".join(WORDS * 6), "long  double  spaces " + " ".join(WORDS * 5), ("word " * 40).strip(), "a" * 90 + " b " + "c" * 90,
    "'" * 50, "tab\t" + " ".join(WORDS * 6), "\\" * 100 + " x " + "y" * 50, "\u00e9" * 100 + " and more words after the long run of letters",
]


def nested(rng: random.Random, depth: int = 0):
    kind = rng.choice(["str", "str", "num", "list", "map", "map"] if depth < 3 else ["str", "num"])
    if kind == "str":
        return rng.choice(TEXTS)
    if kind == "num":
        return rng.choice([0, 1, -5, 3.5, 62.0, 1e-05, 1e17, 26.54, True, False, None, 10 ** 12, -0.0, 0.1 + 0.2])
    if kind == "list":
        return [nested(rng, depth + 1) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 4))]
    return {rng.choice(TEXTS[1:] + ["k", "key two", "max", "fanout:mix"]): nested(rng, depth + 1) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 4))}


def main() -> None:
    rng = random.Random(20261113)
    docs = [{"t": t} for t in TEXTS] + [[t] for t in TEXTS] + [{t: 1} for t in TEXTS] + [{"a": {"b": [t, {"c": t}]}} for t in TEXTS]
    docs += [t for t in TEXTS[:40]] + [1, 2.5, None, True, [], {}, [[]], [{}], {"a": []}, {"a": {}}, [[1, 2], [3, [4, 5]]],
                                       {"a": [[1], {"b": [2, {"c": [3]}]}]}, [{"a": 1, "b": 2}, {"c": [1, 2]}]]
    docs += [nested(rng) for _ in range(400)]
    lock = yaml.safe_load((Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "skills" / "council-loop" / "models" / "lock.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    lock["generated"], lock["data"]["collected"] = str(lock["generated"]), str(lock["data"]["collected"])
    cases = [{"value": d, "width": w, "text": yaml.safe_dump(d, sort_keys=False, width=w)} for d in docs for w in (80, 120)]
    cases.append({"value": lock, "width": 120, "text": yaml.safe_dump(lock, sort_keys=False, width=120)})
    out = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures" / "yaml_dump.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(cases, ensure_ascii=True, allow_nan=False), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{len(cases)} cases -> {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""The codebase skeleton and the checks on a written map."""
import json

import codemap

GOOD_MAP = """# Architecture of shop

> ELI5: a small shop that takes orders and bills each one once.

## Purpose and philosophy
The shop takes orders and bills them once. Money code is small, boring and tested. """ + "It stays small. " * 40 + """

## Bird's-eye view
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  cli --> core --> db
```
Orders come in through `shop/cli.py`, are priced by `shop/core.py` and stored by `shop/db.py`.

## Code map
- `shop/core.py`: pricing and totals. It must not talk to the network.
- `shop/db.py`: storage. `web/app.ts` is the browser side and calls `web/api.ts`.
- `tests/`: the tests. Run state lives in `.council/runs/` and each run has a `run.json`.

## Interfaces
Commands `add` and `bill` in `shop/cli.py`. The variable `SHOP_DB` picks the database. See `<your vault>/index.md`.

## Data and control flow
`cli.py` parses, `core.py` prices, `db.py` saves.

## Invariants
An order is billed at most once.

## Extending it
Add a payment method next to `shop/core.py`.

## Performance and cost
One query per order.

## Where to change what
| To do | Start in |
| --- | --- |
| Change prices | `shop/core.py` |
"""


def make_repo(root):
    (root / "shop").mkdir()
    (root / "web").mkdir()
    (root / "tests").mkdir()
    (root / "shop/__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
    (root / "shop/db.py").write_text('"""Storage for orders."""\nimport os\nimport sqlite3\n\nDB = os.environ.get("SHOP_DB")\n\n\n'
                                    'def save(order):\n    """Write one order."""\n    return 1\n\n\ndef _hidden():\n    return 2\n', encoding="utf-8")
    (root / "shop/core.py").write_text('"""Pricing and totals."""\nfrom shop import db\nfrom . import db as again\nimport requests\n\n\n'
                                      'class Order:\n    """One order."""\n    def total(self):\n        return 3\n\n    def _secret(self):\n        return 0\n\n\n'
                                      'def bill(order: Order, retries: int = 2):\n    """Charge an order once."""\n    return db.save(order)\n', encoding="utf-8")
    (root / "shop/cli.py").write_text('"""The command line."""\nimport argparse\nfrom shop.core import bill\n\n\ndef main():\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n'
                                     '    sub = ap.add_subparsers()\n    sub.add_parser("add")\n    sub.add_parser("bill")\n\n\nif __name__ == "__main__":\n    main()\n', encoding="utf-8")
    (root / "web/api.ts").write_text("export async function getOrders() { return fetch('/orders') }\nexport const VERSION = 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (root / "web/app.ts").write_text("/** The browser app. */\nimport { getOrders } from './api'\nexport class App {}\nconst key = process.env.SHOP_KEY\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (root / "tests/test_core.py").write_text("from shop import core\n\n\ndef test_bill():\n    assert True\n\n\ndef test_total():\n    assert True\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (root / "server.py").write_text('import mcp\n\n@mcp.tool()\ndef shop_bill(order_id: str):\n    """Bill it."""\n    return 1\n\n\n@app.get("/orders")\ndef orders():\n    return []\n', encoding="utf-8")
    (root / "node_modules").mkdir()
    (root / "node_modules/junk.js").write_text("export const x = 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (root / "README.md").write_text("# shop\n", encoding="utf-8")


def test_skeleton_lists_symbols_interfaces_and_who_leans_on_whom(proj):
    make_repo(proj)
    sk = codemap.skeleton(proj)
    md, files = sk["markdown"], sk["scanned"]["files"]
    assert "node_modules/junk.js" not in files and files["shop/core.py"]["doc"] == "Pricing and totals."
    names = [s["name"] for s in files["shop/core.py"]["symbols"]]
    assert names == ["Order", "bill"] and files["shop/core.py"]["symbols"][0]["methods"] == ["total"]
    edges = codemap.resolve_imports(files)
    assert edges["shop/core.py"] == ["shop/db.py"] and edges["shop/cli.py"] == ["shop/core.py"] and edges["web/app.ts"] == ["web/api.ts"]
    assert edges["tests/test_core.py"] == ["shop/core.py"]
    ranked = sorted((n for n in files if files[n]["code"]), key=lambda n: -codemap.rank(files, edges)[n])
    assert ranked[0] == "shop/db.py" and ranked[1] == "shop/core.py"        # everything leans on storage, then pricing
    assert "Commands in `shop/cli.py`: add, bill" in md and "tool shop_bill" in md and "GET /orders" in md
    assert "`SHOP_DB`" in md and "`SHOP_KEY`" in md and "Runnable files (entry points): `shop/cli.py`" in md
    assert "`bill(order: Order, retries: int=2)` · used in 1 other file: Charge an order once." in md
    assert "_hidden" not in md and "_secret" not in md
    assert "requests (1)" in md and "sqlite3" not in md                      # the standard library is not a dependency
    assert "2 test functions in 1 files" in md and sk["stats"]["code_files"] == 8


def test_map_goes_stale_only_when_the_structure_changes(proj):
    make_repo(proj)
    st = codemap.stale(proj)
    assert st["stale"] and "no map yet" in st["reason"]
    path, note = codemap.install_map(GOOD_MAP, proj, run="run-1")
    assert path == proj / "docs" / "ARCHITECTURE.md" and note is None and path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").startswith(codemap.MARKER)
    assert not codemap.stale(proj)["stale"]
    core = proj / "shop/core.py"
    core.write_text(core.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("return db.save(order)", "x = 1\n    return db.save(order)"), encoding="utf-8")
    assert not codemap.stale(proj)["stale"], "a change inside a function body is not a change of structure"
    (proj / "README.md").write_text("# shop, renamed\n", encoding="utf-8")
    assert not codemap.stale(proj)["stale"], "prose does not make the map stale (and the map itself is prose)"
    core.write_text(core.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("retries: int = 2", "retries: int = 2, dry_run: bool = False"), encoding="utf-8")
    st = codemap.stale(proj)
    assert st["stale"] and st["diff"]["changed"] == ["shop/core.py"]
    assert st["reason"].endswith(": shop/core.py"), "the reason names the files, so nobody has to hunt for them"
    (proj / "shop/refunds.py").write_text("def refund():\n    return 0\n", encoding="utf-8")
    assert codemap.stale(proj)["diff"]["added"] == ["shop/refunds.py"]
    assert "new files: `shop/refunds.py`" in codemap.skeleton(proj)["markdown"]
    assert codemap.cmd_map(check=True) == 1 and codemap.cmd_map(accept_now=True) == 0 and codemap.cmd_map(check=True) == 0
    assert json.loads((proj / ".council/map/state.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["structure"]["shop/refunds.py"]


def test_a_new_test_is_not_a_new_structure(proj):
    make_repo(proj)
    codemap.install_map(GOOD_MAP, proj, run="run-1")
    tests = proj / "tests/test_core.py"
    tests.write_text(tests.read_text(encoding="utf-8") + "\n\ndef test_refund():\n    assert True\n\n\nclass TestTotals:\n    def test_sum(self):\n        assert True\n", encoding="utf-8")
    assert not codemap.stale(proj)["stale"], "writing a test must not cost a run of the mapper"
    tests.write_text(tests.read_text(encoding="utf-8") + "\n\ndef make_order():\n    return {}\n", encoding="utf-8")
    st = codemap.stale(proj)
    assert st["stale"] and st["diff"]["changed"] == ["tests/test_core.py"], "a new helper in a test file still counts"
    codemap.accept(proj)
    core = proj / "shop/core.py"
    core.write_text(core.read_text(encoding="utf-8") + "\n\ndef test_connection():\n    return True\n", encoding="utf-8")
    assert codemap.stale(proj)["stale"], "outside test files a name that starts with test_ is an ordinary public name"
    for name, yes in {"tests/test_core.py": True, "pkg/queue_test.go": True, "web/cart.spec.ts": True, "src/__tests__/a.js": True,
                      "conftest.py": True, "shop/core.py": False, "shop/contest.py": False, "attest/keys.py": False}.items():
        assert bool(codemap.TEST_FILE_RX.search(name)) is yes, name


def test_project_without_code_needs_no_map(proj):
    st = codemap.stale(proj)
    assert st == {"applies": False, "stale": False, "reason": "no source code found in this project", "path": st["path"]}


def test_validate_map_checks_sections_and_that_named_paths_exist(proj):
    make_repo(proj)
    errs, warns = codemap.validate_map(GOOD_MAP, proj)
    assert errs == [] and warns == []                       # `.council/…`, bare `run.json` and placeholders are not checked
    errs, _ = codemap.validate_map(GOOD_MAP.replace("## Invariants", "## Rules").replace("## Extending it", "## Growth"), proj)
    assert errs == ["missing section: ## Invariants", "missing section: ## Extending it"]
    invented = GOOD_MAP + "\nSee `shop/payments/stripe.py`, `shop/ledger.py`, `web/checkout.tsx` and `billing.py`.\n"
    errs, _ = codemap.validate_map(invented, proj)
    assert len(errs) == 1 and "shop/ledger.py" in errs[0] and "billing.py" in errs[0] and "shop/core.py" not in errs[0]
    _, warns = codemap.validate_map(GOOD_MAP + "\nAlso `shop/ghost.py`.\n", proj)
    assert warns == ["named in the map but not found: shop/ghost.py"]       # one stray name warns; three or more is an error
    assert codemap.validate_map(GOOD_MAP.replace("> ELI5:", "> Summary:"), proj)[1] == ["no ELI5 line under the title"]
    assert codemap.validate_map("## Purpose and philosophy\nshort", proj)[0][0].startswith("the map is 5 words")
    assert codemap.named_paths("`--drop`, `council.py next`, `https://x.org/a/b`, `skill://a/b.md`, `tests/`, `core.py`") == ["core.py", "tests/"]


def test_install_never_overwrites_a_map_someone_wrote_by_hand(proj):
    make_repo(proj)
    mine = proj / "docs" / "ARCHITECTURE.md"
    mine.write_text("# My own notes\nDo not touch.\n", encoding="utf-8")
    path, note = codemap.install_map(GOOD_MAP, proj)
    assert path.name == "ARCHITECTURE.council.md" and "left alone" in note and mine.read_text(encoding="utf-8").startswith("# My own notes")
    mine.unlink()
    first, _ = codemap.install_map(GOOD_MAP, proj)
    again, note = codemap.install_map(GOOD_MAP.replace("billed at most once", "billed exactly once"), proj)
    assert first == again == mine and note is None and "exactly once" in mine.read_text(encoding="utf-8")      # its own map may be replaced
    assert mine.read_text(encoding="utf-8").count(codemap.MARKER) == 1

def test_a_map_can_be_installed_by_hand_and_a_bad_one_is_refused(proj, capsys):
    make_repo(proj)
    draft = proj / "draft.md"
    draft.write_text("```markdown\n" + GOOD_MAP + "\n```\n", encoding="utf-8")                 # a fence around the whole document is dropped

    assert codemap.cmd_map(install=str(draft)) == 1 and "not installed" in capsys.readouterr().out

def test_ranking_follows_uses_of_names_and_ignores_comments_and_strings(proj):
    """The method of aider's repo map: an edge from the file that uses a name to the file that defines it."""
    make_repo(proj)
    files = codemap.scan(proj)["files"]
    assert "orders" not in files["shop/db.py"]["uses"]           # "Storage for orders." is a docstring, not a use of orders()
    assert "orders" not in files["web/api.ts"]["uses"]           # fetch('/orders') is a string
    assert files["shop/cli.py"]["uses"] == {"bill": 1, "main": 1}
    res = codemap.ranking(files, codemap.resolve_imports(files))
    assert res["used_by"][("shop/core.py", "bill")] == 1 and res["used_by"][("web/api.ts", "getOrders")] == 1
    assert res["names"][("shop/db.py", "save")] > res["names"][("server.py", "orders")]    # used beats unused
    assert res["score"]["server.py"] < res["score"]["shop/core.py"]         # a file nothing uses does not rise by being isolated
    assert codemap.well_named("get_orders") and codemap.well_named("getOrders") and not codemap.well_named("bill")


def test_focus_map_puts_what_the_ask_names_first_and_keeps_to_its_budget(proj):
    make_repo(proj)
    fm = codemap.focus_map(proj, "Change how bill charges an Order; start in shop/cli.py", budget_tokens=120)
    lines = fm["markdown"].splitlines()
    assert lines[0] == "- `shop/cli.py` (named in the ask)" and fm["mentioned"] == ["Order", "bill", "shop"]
    assert lines[2] == "- `shop/core.py`" and "bill(order: Order" in lines[3] and "class Order" in lines[4]
    assert fm["tokens"] <= 120
    small = codemap.focus_map(proj, "anything", budget_tokens=30)
    assert 0 < small["tokens"] <= 30 and len(small["markdown"].splitlines()) < len(lines)
    assert codemap.focus_map(proj / "docs", "x")["markdown"] == ""            # no code, no map


def test_tree_sitter_is_optional_and_never_changes_what_counts_as_structure(proj, monkeypatch):
    pack, have = codemap.tree_sitter()
    if not pack or "go" not in have:

"""Parity: the Rust binary and the Python reference must print the same lines and write the same
files for the same steps.

Each scenario is a list of steps (commands, and files a person or a seat would write in between).
It is played twice, once per implementation, in two fresh folders with the clock frozen. Then every
line printed and every file written is compared. A third play alternates the two implementations
step by step inside ONE project, to show that a run started by either can be finished by the other.

Skipped when the binary is not built: `cargo build --release` (or point COUNCIL_BIN at one).
"""
import difflib
import http.server
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
import yaml

import sim

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CLI = ROOT / "skills" / "council-loop" / "scripts" / "council.py"
BIN = Path(os.environ.get("COUNCIL_BIN") or ROOT / "target" / "release" / ("council.exe" if os.name == "nt" else "council"))
pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not BIN.exists(), reason="the Rust binary is not built: cargo build --release")

# Lines that name the implementation itself. Everything else must match to the letter.
OWN = re.compile(r'^\s*"(?:python|council)": "[^"]*",?\n', re.M)
SCRATCH = re.compile(r'(-o |")[^\s"]+last\.txt')                # the codex adapter's scratch file: its folder is random
SCRUB = ("COUNCIL_", "CLAUDECODE", "OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "AA_API_KEY", "PYTHONIOENCODING")


class World:
    """One project folder and one home folder, driven through one implementation (or both in turn)."""

    def __init__(self, impl: str, base: Path):
        self.impl, self.base = impl, base
        self.root, self.home = base / "proj", base / "home"
        self.root.mkdir(parents=True)
        self.clock, self.log, self.turn = 0, [], 0
        self.always: dict = {}                                   # environment for every command in this world
        self.cli = CLI                                           # the Python entry point (a scenario may run a copy)

    # -- running commands
    def env(self, extra: dict | None = None) -> dict:
        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith(SCRUB)}
        self.clock += 1
        env.update(COUNCIL_HOME=str(self.home / ".council"), CLAUDECODE="1", PYTHONHASHSEED="0",
                   COUNCIL_NOW=f"2026-11-13T12:{self.clock // 60:02d}:{self.clock % 60:02d}",
                   COUNCIL_SKILL_DIR=str(ROOT / "skills" / "council-loop"), COUNCIL_PRIVATE_DIR=str(self.base / "private"),
                   COUNCIL_PARSERS="built-in")
        for key, value in {**self.always, **(extra or {})}.items():    # None = not set at all
            env.pop(key, None) if value is None else env.__setitem__(key, str(value))
        return env

    def c(self, *args, cwd: Path | None = None, env: dict | None = None, loose: bool = False):
        """Run one command. `loose`: the wording of the error may differ (a usage error, a crash); only
        the exit code is compared."""
        order = {"py": ("py",), "rs": ("rs",), "py-rs": ("py", "rs"), "rs-py": ("rs", "py")}[self.impl]
        impl = order[self.turn % len(order)]
        self.turn += 1
        cmd = [sys.executable, str(self.cli)] if impl == "py" else [str(BIN)]
        # arguments go as UTF-8 bytes where the system allows it, so this harness also runs under a locale that is not UTF-8
        argv = [str(a) if os.name == "nt" else str(a).encode("utf-8") for a in args]
        p = subprocess.run(cmd + argv, cwd=cwd or self.root, env=self.env(env), capture_output=True)
        out, err = p.stdout.decode("utf-8"), p.stderr.decode("utf-8")
        self.log.append({"cmd": " ".join(self.norm(str(a)) for a in args), "rc": p.returncode, "out": self.norm(out),
                         "err": "" if loose else self.norm(err)})
        return p.returncode, out, err

    def norm(self, text: str) -> str:
        for path, name in ((self.root, "<ROOT>"), (self.home, "<HOME>"), (self.base, "<BASE>")):
            # a Windows path has its backslashes doubled inside quotes ('C:\\x') and again inside JSON:
            # every spelling names the same folder
            plain = str(path)
            for spelling in (plain.replace("\\", "\\" * 4), plain.replace("\\", "\\" * 2), plain):
                text = text.replace(spelling, name)
            if "\\" in plain:                                    # typed with forward slashes: a spelling of its own, so
                text = text.replace(plain.replace("\\", "/"), name[:-1] + " typed with />")   # that C:/x against C:\x shows
        return SCRATCH.sub(r"<SCRATCH>/last.txt", OWN.sub("", text))

    # -- the world between commands
    def write(self, rel: str, text: str, where: Path | None = None) -> Path:
        f = (where or self.root) / rel
        f.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        f.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        return f

    def read(self, rel: str) -> str:
        return (self.root / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    def run_dir(self) -> Path:
        runs = self.root / ".council" / "runs"
        return runs / (runs / "CURRENT").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()

    def run(self) -> dict:
        return json.loads((self.run_dir() / "run.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    def snapshot(self) -> dict:
        out = {}
        for top in (self.root, self.home, self.base / "private", self.base / "vault", self.base / "skill" / "models"):
            for f in sorted(top.rglob("*")) if top.exists() else []:
                if not f.is_file() or ".git" in f.relative_to(top).parts or "__pycache__" in f.parts:
                    continue
                name = self.norm(str(f))
                try:
                    text = self.norm(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                except UnicodeDecodeError:
                    out[name] = f"<{f.stat().st_size} bytes>"
                    continue
                if f.suffix == ".json":
                    try:
                        out[name] = json.loads(text)
                        continue
                    except ValueError:
                        pass
                out[name] = text                                 # YAML and Markdown: the same bytes, not just the same meaning
        return out


def show(value) -> list[str]:
    text = value if isinstance(value, str) else json.dumps(value, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, default=str)
    return text.splitlines()


def same(a, b, what: str) -> None:
    """Fail with a readable diff: Python's side is `-`, Rust's is `+`."""
    if a == b:
        return
    diff = list(difflib.unified_diff(show(a), show(b), "python", "rust", lineterm="", n=2))
    pytest.fail(f"{what} differs:\n" + "\n".join(diff[:140]), pytrace=False)


def compare(py: World, rs: World) -> None:
    for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(py.log, rs.log)):
        for key in ("rc", "out", "err"):
            same(a[key], b[key], f"step {i + 1} `{a['cmd']}`: {key}")
    sa, sb = py.snapshot(), rs.snapshot()
    same(sorted(sa), sorted(sb), "the list of files written")
    for name in sa:
        same(sa[name], sb[name], f"file {name}")

def fake_aa() -> str:
    """A local stand-in for the Artificial Analysis API, shaped the way the kit reads it (the real one
    is not reachable from a test). `/models` answers 404 and `/models/free` answers, as on the free tier."""
    if _FAKE_AA:
        return _FAKE_AA[0]
    snap = json.loads((ROOT / "skills" / "council-loop" / "models" / "snapshot-2026-11-13.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    rows = []
    for i, m in enumerate(snap["models"]):
        row = {"name": m["name"], "slug": m["name"].lower().replace(" ", "-"), "model_creator": {"name": m["creator"]},
               "evaluations": {"artificial_analysis_intelligence_index": m.get("quality")},
               "performance_v3": {"time_per_task_seconds": (m.get("minutes") or 0) * 60},
               "licensing": {"is_open_weights": bool(m.get("open_weights"))}, "trusted_access": i == 0,
               "openrouter_api_id": f"lab/{i}" if i % 3 == 0 else None}
        if i % 4 == 1:                                           # some rows carry only a blended token price
            row["pricing"] = {"price_1m_blended_3_to_1": m.get("cost_per_task")}
        else:
            row["artificial_analysis_intelligence_index_cost"] = {"cost_per_task": {"total_cost": m.get("cost_per_task")}}
        rows.append(row)
    rows.append({"slug": "no-name-no-data"})
    body = json.dumps({"status": 200, "data": rows}).encode()

    class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def do_GET(self):                                        # noqa: N802
            ok = self.path == "/models/free" and self.headers.get("x-api-key") == "test-key"
            self.send_response(200 if ok else 401 if self.path == "/models/free" else 404)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body if ok else b'{"error": "no"}')

        def log_message(self, *args):
            pass

    server = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
    threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
    _FAKE_AA.append(f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_address[1]}")
    return _FAKE_AA[0]

def brief(w: World, **changes) -> None:
    """The chair's intent brief, filled in the way a person or a model would."""
    run = w.run()
    experts = sorted(s for s, v in run["seats"].items() if v["role"] == "expert")
    data = {"restated": "Pick the queue technology for the billing pipeline.", "eli5": "choose the safest mail system",
            "rubric": [{"id": f"R{i + 1}", "name": n, "weight": wt, "check": "judgment"} for i, (n, wt) in enumerate(
                [("reliability", 40), ("cost", 20), ("simplicity", 20), ("speed to ship", 10), ("operability", 10)])],
            "evidence_plan": ["load test"],
            "lenses": [{"id": s, "name": f"lens {s[1:]}", "maximize": "one thing", "respect": "a limit",
                        "method": "first principles", "evidence": "facts"} for s in experts],
            "facts": "Peak is 4,000 events per second.", "lessons_applied": ["L-20261113-1"], "approved_by": "requester"}
    data.update(changes)
    w.write("brief.yaml", yaml.safe_dump(data, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True), where=w.run_dir())


def act(w: World, prompt_file: Path, mode: str = "ok", target: str | None = None) -> Path:
    """One seat answers its packet. The answer is worked out from the packet with this world's folders
    named as every world names them, so two worlds get the same answer to the same packet."""
    prompt = prompt_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    out = sim.out_path(prompt)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if "· CODEBASE MAP ·" in prompt:
        text = sim.codebase_map(prompt, mode)
        out.write_text("```markdown\n" + text + "\n```\n" if mode == "fenced" else text, encoding="utf-8")
        return out
    text = json.dumps(sim.answer(w.norm(prompt), "ok" if mode == "fenced" else mode, target))
    out.write_text("Here is my answer:\n```json\n" + text + "\n```\n" if mode == "fenced" else text, encoding="utf-8")
    return out


def seats(w: World, step: str, mode: str = "ok", target: str | None = None, only: tuple = (), skip: tuple = ()) -> None:
    """Every seat of a step answers (`step` is like "loop-1/ideate")."""
    for prompt in sorted((w.run_dir() / step).glob("*.prompt.md")):
        seat = prompt.name.split(".")[0]
        if (only and seat not in only) or seat in skip:
            continue
        act(w, prompt, mode, target)


def control(w: World, mode: str = "ok") -> None:
    act(w, w.run_dir() / "control" / "CTRL.prompt.md", mode)


def edit(w: World, rel: str, change) -> None:
    """The chair edits one of its JSON files."""
    f = w.run_dir() / rel
    obj = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    obj = change(obj) or obj
    f.write_text(json.dumps(obj, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")


def approve_pool(w: World, k: int) -> None:
    edit(w, f"loop-{k}/pool.json", lambda o: o.update(reviewed=True))


def fill_fuse(w: World, k: int, action: str = "fixed", note: str = "added idempotency keys to every consumer", checks: dict | None = None) -> None:
    def change(o):
        for r in o["responses"]:
            r.update(action=action, note=note)
        o["checks"] = checks or {}
    edit(w, f"loop-{k}/candidates.json", change)


def research(w: World, k: int = 1, mode: str = "ok") -> None:
    if w.run()["phase"] == "research":
        seats(w, f"loop-{k}/research", mode)
        w.c("ingest")


def to_cut(w: World, k: int, ideate: str = "ok", vote: str = "ok", rank: str = "ok", elders: str = "ok", target: str | None = None,
           checks: dict | None = None) -> None:
    """One loop, from the ideas to the cut."""
    seats(w, f"loop-{k}/ideate", ideate)
    if k == 1:
        control(w)
    w.c("ingest")                                                # -> merge
    approve_pool(w, k)
    w.c("ingest")                                                # -> shortlist vote, or straight to the red team
    if w.run()["phase"] == "vote":
        seats(w, f"loop-{k}/vote", vote)
        w.c("ingest")
    seats(w, f"loop-{k}/redteam")
    w.c("ingest")                                                # -> fuse
    fill_fuse(w, k, checks=checks)
    w.c("ingest")                                                # -> rank vote
    seats(w, f"loop-{k}/rank", rank)
    w.c("ingest")                                                # -> elders
    seats(w, f"loop-{k}/elders", elders, target)
    w.c("ingest")                                                # -> cut


def finish(w: World) -> None:
    """The chair writes the final and the retro."""
    d = w.run_dir()
    final = d / "final.md"
    final.write_text(final.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("TODO(chair)", "done") +
                     "\nDecided unattended where noted. Stand-in seats are labelled. The control baseline was read.\n", encoding="utf-8")
    w.c("ingest")                                                # -> retro
    retro = d / "retro.md"
    retro.write_text(retro.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("TODO(chair)", "done").replace(
        "they reach docs/lessons.md only through a PR)",
        "they reach docs/lessons.md only through a PR)\n- [L-20261114-1] (helpful: 0 | harmful: 0) Lock the tests first. Evidence: this run"),
        encoding="utf-8")
    w.c("ingest")                                                # -> done


def at(w: World, phase: str) -> None:
    """Guard: a scenario that silently stopped moving would compare equal for the wrong reason."""
    run = w.run()
    assert run["phase"] == phase, f"expected {phase}, at {run['phase']} after `{w.log[-1]['cmd']}`:\n{w.log[-1]['out']}{w.log[-1]['err']}"

def ascii_env(**extra) -> dict:
    """An interpreter whose default text encoding is ASCII: no arrow, no accent, nothing above 127."""
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k not in ("PYTHONIOENCODING", "LC_CTYPE", "LANGUAGE", "CLAUDECODE")}
    env.update(LC_ALL="C", LANG="C", PYTHONUTF8="0", PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE="0", **extra)
    return env


def cli(args, cwd, **env):
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(CLI), *args], cwd=cwd, env=ascii_env(**env), capture_output=True)
    out, err = p.stdout.decode("utf-8"), p.stderr.decode("utf-8")       # strict: whatever is printed is UTF-8
    assert "Traceback" not in err and "codec can't" not in err, err
    return p.returncode, out, err


def unsafe_calls(path: Path):
    """Calls that would read or write text in the machine's own encoding."""
    for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))):
        if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
            continue
        f, kw = node.func, {k.arg for k in node.keywords}
        attr = f.attr if isinstance(f, ast.Attribute) else None
        base = getattr(getattr(f, "value", None), "id", "")
        if attr == "read_text" and not node.args and "encoding" not in kw:
            yield node.lineno, "read_text() without an encoding"
        elif attr == "write_text" and len(node.args) == 1 and "encoding" not in kw:
            yield node.lineno, "write_text() without an encoding"
        elif (isinstance(f, ast.Name) and f.id == "open") or (attr == "open" and base not in ("os", "webbrowser", "tarfile", "zipfile")):
            at = 1 if isinstance(f, ast.Name) else 0
            mode = node.args[at] if len(node.args) > at else next((k.value for k in node.keywords if k.arg == "mode"), None)
            if not (isinstance(mode, ast.Constant) and "b" in str(mode.value)) and "encoding" not in kw:
                yield node.lineno, "open() in text mode without an encoding"
        elif base == "subprocess" and attr in ("run", "Popen", "check_output", "check_call", "call"):
            texty = any(k.arg in ("text", "universal_newlines") and getattr(k.value, "value", False) for k in node.keywords)
            if texty and "encoding" not in kw:
                yield node.lineno, f"subprocess.{attr}(text=True) without an encoding"

# Where a file may be written without the guard, and why.
WRITES_OF_THEIR_OWN = {
    ("council.py", "write_text"): "the guard itself", ("council.py", "make_dir"): "the guard itself",
    ("council.py", "private_file"): "the guard itself",
    ("refresh_models.py", "load_live"): "model data in the skill folder", ("refresh_models.py", "main"): "the path given with --out",

def test_every_file_goes_through_one_writer_and_every_line_ends_the_same_way():
    """One function writes this kit's files: council.write_text. It fixes the encoding and the line ends
    (text mode on Windows would write \\r\\n where the Rust binary writes \\n) and it refuses to write
    through a link or outside the project. A direct write anywhere else would skip all three, so the
    source is read here: the effect of a missing guard only shows on a hostile repository."""
    found = []
    for p in SHIPPED:
        tree = ast.parse(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        owner = {}
        for fn in ast.walk(tree):
            if isinstance(fn, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
                for node in ast.walk(fn):
                    owner.setdefault(id(node), fn.name)
        for node in ast.walk(tree):
            if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
                continue
            f, where = node.func, f"{p.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()}:{node.lineno}"
            newline = next((getattr(k.value, "value", None) for k in node.keywords if k.arg == "newline"), None)
            if isinstance(f, ast.Attribute) and f.attr == "reconfigure" and newline != "\n":
                found.append(f'{where}: reconfigure() without newline="\\n"')
            direct = (isinstance(f, ast.Attribute) and f.attr in ("write_text", "write_bytes", "mkdir", "makedirs")
                      and getattr(f.value, "id", "") != "council") or (isinstance(f, ast.Name) and f.id == "open")
            if not direct:
                continue
            if (p.name, owner.get(id(node))) not in WRITES_OF_THEIR_OWN:
                found.append(f"{where}: {getattr(f, 'attr', 'open')}() outside council.write_text / council.make_dir")
            elif getattr(f, "attr", "") == "write_text" and newline != "\n":
                found.append(f'{where}: write_text() without newline="\\n"')
    assert not found, "\n".join(found)
    for script in (CLI, SCRIPTS / "refresh_models.py", HOOK):       # every entry point sets up its console
        assert "reconfigure(" in script.read_text(encoding="utf-8") or "utf8_console()" in script.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), script

def test_a_tool_behind_a_cmd_file_is_run_by_its_full_path_and_read_as_utf8(monkeypatch):
    seen = {}

    def fake_run(cmd, **kw):
        seen.update(cmd=cmd, kw=kw)
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 0, stdout='{"ok": "naïve → fine"}\r\nsecond line\r\n'.encode("utf-8"), stderr=b"")

    monkeypatch.setattr(providers.shutil, "which", lambda name: rf"C:\Users\me\AppData\Roaming\npm\{name}.cmd")
    monkeypatch.setattr(providers.subprocess, "run", fake_run)
    res = providers.ask("openai", "Read and follow the packet\nline two → three", timeout=5)
    assert seen["cmd"][0].endswith("codex.cmd"), "npm installs codex and gemini as .cmd files on Windows"
    # bytes both ways: a text pipe would write \r\n for every \n of the prompt on Windows and read the reply as cp1252
    assert seen["kw"]["input"] == "Read and follow the packet\nline two → three".encode("utf-8")
    assert not {"text", "encoding", "universal_newlines"} & set(seen["kw"])
    assert res["ok"] and "→" in res["text"] and "\r" not in res["text"]

def current() -> tuple[dict, Path]:

def start(tier="lite", mode="fanout:claude", ask="Pick a queue for billing events", loops=None, profile="balanced",
          research=None, mapper=None, through_research=True, obsidian=False, paths=(), **settings):
    runner.cmd_init(ask, tier, mode, profile, loops, list(paths), None, None, None, research, mapper, obsidian, **settings)
    run, d = current()
    write_brief(d, run)
    runner.cmd_ingest()
    if through_research:
        do_research(d)
    return current()


def do_research(d: Path, k: int = 1, mode="ok"):
    """Play the researchers (and the mapper, when it is due) if the run is at that step."""
    run, _ = current()
    if run["phase"] != "research":
        return
    if any(v["via"].startswith("cli:") for v in run["seats"].values()):
        runner.cmd_dispatch()                                # seats behind a command-line tool answer through it
    else:
        sim.act_all(d, f"loop-{k}/research/*.prompt.md", mode)
    runner.cmd_ingest()


def write_brief(d: Path, run: dict):
    brief = {"restated": "Pick the queue technology for the billing pipeline.", "eli5": "choose the safest mail system",
             "rubric": [{"id": f"R{i + 1}", "name": n, "weight": w, "check": "judgment"}
                        for i, (n, w) in enumerate([("reliability", 40), ("cost", 20), ("simplicity", 20),
                                                    ("speed to ship", 10), ("operability", 10)])],
             "evidence_plan": ["load test"],
             "lenses": [{"id": s, "name": f"lens {s[1:]}", "maximize": "one thing", "respect": "a limit",
                         "method": "first principles", "evidence": "facts"} for s in runner.seats_of(run, "expert")],
             "facts": "Peak is 4,000 events per second.", "lessons_applied": ["L-20261113-1"], "approved_by": "requester"}
    (d / "brief.yaml").write_text(yaml.safe_dump(brief), encoding="utf-8")


def fill_fuse(d: Path, k: int):
    f = d / f"loop-{k}" / "candidates.json"
    obj = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    for r in obj["responses"]:
        r.update(action="fixed", note="added idempotency keys to every consumer")
    f.write_text(json.dumps(obj), encoding="utf-8")


def approve_pool(d: Path, k: int):
    f = d / f"loop-{k}" / "pool.json"
    obj = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    obj["reviewed"] = True
    f.write_text(json.dumps(obj), encoding="utf-8")


def to_fuse(d: Path, k: int, ideate_mode="ok"):
    sim.act_all(d, f"loop-{k}/ideate/*.prompt.md", ideate_mode)
    if k == 1:
        sim.act(d / "control" / "CTRL.prompt.md")
    runner.cmd_ingest()                                      # -> merge
    approve_pool(d, k)
    runner.cmd_ingest()                                      # -> vote or redteam
    if current()[0]["phase"] == "vote":
        sim.act_all(d, f"loop-{k}/vote/*.prompt.md")
        runner.cmd_ingest()
    sim.act_all(d, f"loop-{k}/redteam/*.prompt.md")
    runner.cmd_ingest()                                      # -> fuse


def one_loop(d: Path, k: int, elder_mode="ok", target=None, ideate_mode="ok", vote_mode="ok"):
    to_fuse(d, k, ideate_mode)
    fill_fuse(d, k)
    runner.cmd_ingest()                                      # -> rank
    sim.act_all(d, f"loop-{k}/rank/*.prompt.md", vote_mode)
    runner.cmd_ingest()                                      # -> elders
    sim.act_all(d, f"loop-{k}/elders/*.prompt.md", elder_mode, target)
    runner.cmd_ingest()                                      # -> cut


def finish(d: Path):
    f = d / "final.md"
    f.write_text(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("TODO(chair)", "done") + "\nDecided unattended where noted. stand-in seats are labelled.\n", encoding="utf-8")
    runner.cmd_ingest()                                      # -> retro
    r = d / "retro.md"
    text = r.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("TODO(chair)", "done").replace(
        "they reach docs/lessons.md only through a PR)",
        "they reach docs/lessons.md only through a PR)\n- [L-20261114-1] (helpful: 0 | harmful: 0) Lock the tests first. Evidence: this run")
    r.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    runner.cmd_ingest()                                      # -> done

def field(obj, *names):
    """A field of an SDK object, whichever of its spellings this SDK version uses."""
    for name in names:
        if hasattr(obj, name):
            return getattr(obj, name)
    raise AttributeError(names[0])


async def play_mcp(w: World) -> dict:
    """Connect to one implementation's server and drive it. Returns what it offers and every answer."""
    from mcp import ClientSession, StdioServerParameters
    from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client

    env = w.env({"COUNCIL_NOW": "2026-11-13T12:00:00"})          # one clock for the whole session
    command, args = (sys.executable, [str(SERVER)]) if w.impl == "py" else (str(BIN), ["mcp"])
    log: list[dict] = []
    async with stdio_client(StdioServerParameters(command=command, args=args, env=env, cwd=str(w.root))) as (r, wr):
        async with ClientSession(r, wr) as s:
            init = await s.initialize()

            async def call(name: str, **kw) -> dict:
                out = await s.call_tool(name, kw)
                failed = bool(field(out, "is_error", "isError"))
                text = out.content[0].text
                answer = None if failed else json.loads(text)      # a refused call is worded by each SDK in its own way
                if not failed:
                    structured = field(out, "structured_content", "structuredContent")
                    assert structured is None or structured == answer, f"{name}: the text and the structured answer differ"
                log.append({"cmd": f"{name} {json.dumps(kw, sort_keys=True)[:90]}", "rc": int(failed),
                            "out": w.norm(json.dumps(answer, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)), "err": ""})
                return answer if isinstance(answer, dict) else {}

            tools = field(await s.list_tools(), "tools")
            resources = field(await s.list_resources(), "resources")
            templates = field(await s.list_resource_templates(), "resource_templates", "resourceTemplates")
            prompts = field(await s.list_prompts(), "prompts")
            offered = {"protocol": field(init, "protocol_version", "protocolVersion"),
                       "tools": [t.model_dump(mode="json", by_alias=True, exclude_none=True) for t in tools],
                       "resources": [x.model_dump(mode="json", by_alias=True, exclude_none=True) for x in resources],
                       "templates": [x.model_dump(mode="json", by_alias=True, exclude_none=True) for x in templates],
